summary: The project has built a very safe, well-audited rule-based chat agent (0 wrong saves in 360 red-team turns; sealed runs; honest FAIL records). But almost all of that work now goes into a growing pile of hand-written English rules. The current base pulls in 122 script modules (about 39,000 lines, 292 regex call sites). It still fails most everyday rewordings: in my probe, 0 of 13 reworded questions were answered, while the canonical forms of the same questions worked. The own-weights model cannot inherit these rules as they stand. The learned parts that could replace them (ears, talker) are aimed at other targets: ears at encyclopedia reading (0 real saves so far), the talker at grammar scores. None of them is aimed at the chat turns Ben actually types. The benchmark and demo evidence is real but thin for an expert: the 100/100 MQuAKE result used gold triples or template English, a single question wording per case, and conflicting cases were dropped. The plain-transformer baseline in the demo has 128k parameters. My recommendation is to freeze the rule loop and use it as a teacher and test suite, point the learned reader at chat turns, and spend the rest of the effort on one demo script and one tougher benchmark run.

findings.title: Rule-patch treadmill: every fix is a new hand-written rule the final model can't inherit
findings.problem: Nearly every recent piece (138b-138i, layer C, the QUEUED list) adds one more English phrase rule: tail words, hearsay adverbs, lowercase names, 'Say what?', 'Tell me again who...'. Each probe finds new gaps, so the list never shrinks. These rules exist only as Python code, so a from-scratch model gains nothing from them unless they are turned into training data. That is the opposite of 'Ben's own genuinely-learning model'.
findings.evidence: Transitive imports of scripts/fable_loop138i_agent.py: 122 modules, 39,164 lines, 292 regex call sites (my import-walk script). Board 'QUEUED for after layer C' and 'Overnight fixes' list about 40 phrase-level fixes (design/v3/30-modes/00-director-board.md:8-9, 275-310). Probe on 138i (fresh notebook): after 'Tavi's boss is Moren.' + 'Moren lives in Quellport.', these all failed: 'Where does Tavi's boss live?', 'Tavi reports to whom?', 'Who lives in Quellport?', 'Where is Brisa's boss from?', 'What do you know about Kolt?'. 'Rundel has a sister named Fenn.' was not understood. Control: 'What is Tavi's boss's city?' -> 'Tavi's boss's city is Quellport.' and 'Where does Moren live?' works. Some of these (190 reverse, 164 about) are waiting in layer C, but the pattern holds.
findings.improvement: Freeze the rule loop at 138i/138j for new phrase rules. Keep it as (1) the safety shell (write guards, notebook contract, daemon) and (2) a labeller: run it plus Qwen-written paraphrases (already allowed by the ears decisions) over large generated chat sets to produce (utterance -> frame) training pairs. Only pairs where the rule loop and the Qwen listener agree count as silver labels; disagreements go to review. Turn every existing red-team and regression suite into the learned parser's test set. From then on a new phrasing is fixed by adding training examples, not code.
findings.expected_gain: Rewording coverage grows with data instead of with agent-hours. The rules' value carries over into Ben's own weights. This removes the main mismatch with the own-architecture goal.
findings.risk: A learned parser will make some confident wrong writes that the rules never made. Keep every existing write guard in front of it, and keep 'wrong writes = 0' as the gate. Silver labels can copy the rule loop's blind spots. Qwen paraphrases are a weaker check than Ben's own words.

findings.title: Point the learned ears at chat turns, not encyclopedia reading
findings.problem: The GPU and most of the ears effort (119 through 119h) target reading real encyclopedia sentences. That is a hard open-domain relation-extraction task, and it is still a registered FAIL with 0 real saves. Ben's first priority is conversation. The benchmarks (MQuAKE edits and questions, reversal, abstention) are short, cloze-style sentences much closer to chat turns than to Wikipedia prose.
findings.evidence: Morning report: ears119 'Real sentences: still 0 saves on all 3 seeds'; relation wrong 224/312; confidence upside down (correct reads max 0.52 vs save bar 0.96). 119g is 3.4-4.3x better but still FAIL (00-morning-report-20260922.md). The board shows 119h on the GPU now (00-director-board.md:6). Benchmark sentences are cloze-style edits (design/v3/30-modes/63-benchmark-plan-research-muse.md section 1).
findings.improvement: After 119h finishes, move the ears target to the chat-and-benchmark distribution. Input: user turns plus MQuAKE-style edit sentences and questions. Output: the notebook frame (teach / ask / correct / chain question / small talk / unknown), with relations mapped to one canonical name. Park encyclopedia reading, which belongs to the later 'reading ladder' milestone.
findings.expected_gain: One learned component that serves the talk goal, the demo and the benchmark at once, instead of none of them yet.
findings.risk: The borrowed encoder is allowed only for now; the own encoder must later be trained on the same marks. It could overfit to generated chat phrasing, so use held-out paraphrase authors.

findings.title: Relations are surface words, not concepts (boss is not employer)
findings.problem: The notebook stores each English phrasing as its own relation. Facts taught one way can't be found when asked another way. This hurts teachability and makes benchmark paraphrase questions fail. More phrase rules can't fix it; a canonical relation layer (learned or table-based) can.
findings.evidence: Probe on 138i: 'Tavi's boss is Moren.' then 'Who is Tavi's employer?' -> 'I don't know Tavi's employer.'. 'Brisa's employer is Kolt.' then 'Who is Brisa's boss?' -> 'I don't know Brisa's boss.' Also 'Brisa works for Kolt.' is saved as employer, but 'Where is Brisa's boss from?' -> "I don't know Brisa's boss from."
findings.improvement: Add one canonical relation vocabulary with alias sets (boss/manager/employer/works for; lives in/city/home). Use it both as the learned parser's output labels and as a lookup step in the notebook. Short term, a hand-built alias table is a data file the learned parser can later absorb. Keep taught wording for replies.
findings.expected_gain: Fixes a whole class of 'I don't know' answers after correct teaching. Needed for MQuAKE's 3 paraphrased questions per case.
findings.risk: Merging relations that aren't really the same (boss vs employer company). Keep ambiguous merges as 'ask Ben', never silent.

findings.title: The benchmark result is not yet expert-grade; make one hard, honest run
findings.problem: The headline 100/100 MQuAKE two-hop comes from gold triples (bench65) or a template English arm (bench73) whose templates were written for the same data. Only the first of MQuAKE's 3 question wordings is used. The batch split dropped 76 conflicting cases (bench103). An expert will call this 'oracle facts plus a symbolic lookup', which is known to beat weight editing (MeLLo, RAG). The respected part would be showing that Ben's learned parts do the reading.
findings.evidence: artifacts/fable-bench65-20260921/RESULTS.md: 'This arm feeds TRIPLES, not English'. scripts/fable_bench65_build.py:137 'question': L(r['questions'])[0] (first wording only). artifacts/fable-bench103-20260921/RESULTS.md: 924/924 after 'Dropped 76 cases'. bench92 English S2 142/32/26 before fixes. Baseline bench66: SmolLM2-360M in-context 52/150, RAG-lite 38/150, abstention wrong 43/50.
findings.improvement: Register one run, 'MQuAKE-Remastered CF-3k batch': teach all edits and needed chain facts for all 3k cases into one notebook as English sentences (a large distractor pool). Ask all 3 question wordings per case, parsed by the learned parser from the ears change above. Report conflicting cases as their own row instead of dropping them. Baselines: SmolLM2-360M in-context and RAG (existing bench66 harness), plus a MeLLo-style decompose-and-retrieve baseline on the same small model. Cite published editor numbers from the Remastered paper, clearly labelled as bigger models. Add the reversal and abstention slices unchanged.
findings.expected_gain: A result an expert can't dismiss as an oracle: a from-scratch-trained reader plus notebook beats equal-size LM+RAG on multi-hop edits at high precision, with abstention.
findings.risk: The score will drop well below 100/100 once real paraphrases and a learned reader are used. That is the honest number and still likely far above 52/150. The harder run depends on the learned parser existing.

findings.title: Demo: freeze a base now and build a guided script with the SmolLM2 side-by-side
findings.problem: Demo pieces exist (demo55 teach/two-hop/forget-vs-baseline; demo126 A1-A8 on the loop; self card 161), but the demo keeps waiting for the next merge layer. Its baseline is a 128k-parameter 2-layer transformer, which a funder's expert friend will not accept as 'a plain transformer'. Live free typing will hit the rewording gaps shown in the probe.
findings.evidence: artifacts/fable-demo55-20260921/RESULTS.md: baseline 128,512 params; notebook 20/20 vs 0/20; 55b forgetting 0/20 old after fine-tune. artifacts/fable-demo126-20260922/RESULTS.md A1-A8 PASS on loop117/113b. Self card 161 misses reworded self questions (S2 14/69, S3 15/100) per morning report. Memory demo-requirements-uncle: 'As of 22 Sep there is NO end-to-end model yet.'
findings.improvement: Freeze 138i (or 138j) as the demo base. Write one guided 10-minute script: knows nothing -> teach 8 facts -> two-hop -> correction propagates -> restart persistence -> 'I don't know' -> self questions in the phrasings the self card handles. Run SmolLM2-360M-Instruct side by side on the same turns (bench66 code) as the equal-size SOTA foil. Keep the tiny transformer only as the forgetting illustration. Show the rewording weakness openly as 'what the learned reader is for'.
findings.expected_gain: The demo becomes ready in days instead of waiting on endless merge layers, and the comparison holds up.
findings.risk: A guided script can look staged. Say plainly that the listener is hand-written for now. The rule loop is Ben's own software, so it does not break the 'own architecture' rule.

findings.title: Lighten the process for plain-software phrase fixes
findings.problem: Full seal, ledger predictions and registered-FAIL rules are applied to one-line phrase fixes. Many FAILs were procedure faults rather than feature failures (code edited after the seal, wrong base named, an unpredicted improvement). Each costs a re-run cycle. The outside review already accepted 'lighter manifests for cheap diagnostics'.
findings.evidence: Morning report: '180 and 187 (code edited after the seal), 170 (the mark named the wrong base), 167c (an improvement nobody predicted)' stay FAIL. The 138d/138f/138g/138h/138i merge chain is about 5 layers in one day. design/v3/28-outside-review-adjudication-fable.md accepted lighter manifests (per memory outside-review-28-adjudication).
findings.improvement: Keep full registration for learned-model experiments and benchmark runs. For deterministic software fixes, use a lighter tier: regression suite green plus the new cases, with no ledger prediction.
findings.expected_gain: Frees agent and director time for the learned parser and the benchmark.
findings.risk: Slightly weaker audit trail for software changes. Keep the wrong-write gate mandatory.

findings.title: Pause parked tracks that don't serve the three goals
findings.problem: Talker grammar work (BLiMP), THINKING/web/modes, dreamer and further sleep toys compete for attention. None of them is on the shortest path to the demo or the benchmark. Template replies already give 0/500 wrong after the brake.
findings.evidence: Morning report: talker T2 FAIL BLiMP 67.4%, raw unfaithful 172/500 after 120b; safe only because of the brake. Memory outside-review-28-adjudication: 'concept toy, dreamer, web, tools stay parked'. Ben decided the learned talker waits until the template assistant works end to end.
findings.improvement: Pause talker retraining, modes/thinking/web and new sleep toys until the learned parser and the benchmark run land. Keep the existing sleep recipe (exp46) as is.
findings.expected_gain: The limited agent slots, GPU and Ben's attention go to the two deliverables.
findings.risk: Ben values the talker ('wants it to TALK'). Say plainly that the mouth stays template-based for the demo and resumes right after.

keep_as_is: Notebook contract with append-only log, taught-beats-inferred, discrete failure statuses and templated 'I don't know': this is the architectural edge in every comparison (bench65/73 abstention 50/50, 0 wrong).
Write guards and the 0-wrong-writes gate (152: 0 wrong saves in 360 phone turns). Keep them in front of any learned parser.
Sealed registration and 'registered FAIL stays FAIL' for learned experiments and benchmark runs.
The existing baseline harness bench66 (SmolLM2-360M in-context + RAG-lite) and demo55/55b forgetting arm: reuse them, don't rebuild.
Deterministic hop loop (outside review 28): a learned dispatcher is not needed for the demo or the benchmark.
Sleep recipe exp46 (harden-before-gate) as the live consolidation method; no new sleep toys needed right now.
Daemon reliability work (exactly-once 108, settle 141, speed 142).
open_questions_for_ben: For the uncle/dad demo, is a hand-written (rule-based) listener acceptable as 'your own architecture', since it is your own software with no borrowed weights, or must the listener be learned before you show it?
OK to freeze new phrase rules at 138i/138j and turn the rule loop into a teacher that labels training data for a learned chat reader?
OK to pause encyclopedia reading (ears 119 line) after 119h finishes and aim the ears at chat turns and benchmark sentences instead?
For the benchmark, will you accept a lower but tougher number (all 3 MQuAKE question wordings, a learned reader, conflicts reported rather than dropped) over the current 100/100 on templates?

part: Conversation loop: English understanding and replies (loop-parser, loop138i)
summary: Loop138i handles one sentence shape well: "X's REL is Y." / "What is X's REL?". That covers two-hop possessives ("What is Rhea's manager's city?" -> Ghent), corrections that ask first, forget, and name teaching. It also never gave a wrong fact as an answer in my probes. But plain everyday English mostly fails. On my fresh natural-phrasing batch (53 turns, fictional names) it scored 18 OK, 9 wrong or misleading, 26 unhelpful. A second batch leaning on the template scored 29 OK, 1 wrong, 10 unhelpful out of 40. The failures come from pieces that do not combine: each rule piece handles one axis (verb form, possessive chain, "of"-chain, yes/no) with its own sentence-wide regex and its own closed word list. So "Where does Liora live?" works but "Where does my sister live?" does not, and "What is Rhea's manager's city?" works but "What is the city of Rhea's manager?" does not. The stack is now 35 classes deep on the ears side. 109 project modules (about 36,000 lines) load, holding 276 regex call sites. Every new phrasing becomes its own sealed piece, and the director's queue of phrasing gaps is growing faster than merges can close it. The verified layer C pieces (187b, 188, 164b) that I ran on their own agents mostly make the don't-know message clearer. They save almost none of the natural teaches that currently fail.

findings.title: Natural phrasing fails about half the time; failures are combinations of pieces, not missing pieces
findings.problem: The rules understand the canonical template plus a few verb forms. Anything that combines two features (a verb question plus a possessive subject, an of-chain plus a relation outside one piece's list, a yes/no plus a verb, a pronoun, two facts at once) falls through to the don't-know reply. Common teaching shapes also fail: 'is a dentist', 'likes chess and hiking', 'is 34 years old', 'moved to', 'I live in'. So do the matching questions: 'How old is X?', 'What does X do?', 'Who is X married to?'.
findings.evidence: Probe on scripts/fable_loop138i_agent.py with its registered config (ears chain bench73 -> fake), fresh notebooks, 93 turns. Natural batch: OK 18 / wrong 9 / unhelpful 26 (of 53). Template-leaning batch: OK 29 / wrong 1 / unhelpful 10 (of 40). Pairs that show non-composition: 'Where does Liora live?' -> 'Liora's city is Tallinn.' but 'Where does my sister live?' -> glued fallback, although 'What is my sister's city?' -> 'Your sister's city is Tallinn.'. 'What is Rhea's manager's city?' -> 'Ghent' but 'Where does Rhea's manager live?' -> fallback, and 'What is the city of Rhea's manager?' -> 'I don't know anyone called the city of Rhea.'. 'Does Liora work at Brindle Labs?' and 'Is Liora's employer Brindle Labs?' -> fallback. 'She works at Brindle Labs.' -> fallback (no pronouns). 'Kesi's brother is Anwar and Anwar lives in Lagos.' -> 'I can take one fact at a time'. Probe dialogs and outputs: scratchpad wf-loop-parser/dialogs.json, run1.txt, dialogs2.json, run2.txt.
findings.improvement: Replace sentence-wide regexes with one small compositional parse. Step 1: parse the subject noun phrase into a chain ('my sister', 'Rhea's manager', 'the city of Rhea's manager', 'she/he' = last person mentioned) -> list of hops. Step 2: look up the predicate in ONE relation lexicon table: relation -> teach surfaces ('lives in', 'works at', 'is N years old', 'is a <job>', 'likes'), question surfaces ('where does _ live', 'how old is _', 'what does _ do'), yes/no surfaces ('does _ work at', 'is _'s REL V'). Step 3: split on ' and ' between full clauses. Every existing piece's word list moves into that one table. Build it as a fresh piece, parity-tested against the 138i sealed cases (it must reproduce every current reply on the frozen suites) plus a new fresh natural panel.
findings.expected_gain: Most of the 26 unhelpful natural turns come from about 6 predicate shapes x 3 subject shapes, so one table plus a chain parse could plausibly take the natural batch from about 34% OK to 70% or more (SUSPECTED until built). Future phrasing gaps become one table row, not one sealed piece and merge.
findings.risk: A big parity surface: the new parse must reproduce the 138i frozen suites byte for byte or explain each move. Mitigation: run it as the innermost fallback first (it only claims turns the stack drops to the fallback), then promote it layer by layer.

findings.title: Each piece has its own closed relation list, so relations work in one form but not another
findings.problem: 174's of-chain rewrite fires only for 13 hard-coded surfaces (boss, brother, ..., wife, city). 'manager' and 'employer' are missing, which explains the director's 'employer of Ana's boss' failure and my 'city of Rhea's manager' failure. Other pieces keep their own lists too (the 154e multi-value allow-list, PERSON_RELATIONS in fable_agent_loop.py). A relation Ben teaches through the main template is therefore only partly understood in the other forms.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_fix174_chainof.py:34-55 (REL174 frozenset of 13, 'the rewrite fires only for these 13'). Probe: after "Rhea's manager is Dorian." + "Dorian's city is Ghent.": "What is Rhea's manager's city?" -> "Rhea's manager's city is Ghent." but "What is the city of Rhea's manager?" -> "I don't know anyone called the city of Rhea.". 44 of the 109 loaded modules mention 'lives in'/'works at'/'born in' surfaces (grep over loaded module files).
findings.improvement: Short term (one change): let the 174 of-chain accept any relation the notebook already has a RELATION event for (closed by the notebook, not by a code list), instead of REL174. Long term: fold into the single lexicon from finding 1.
findings.expected_gain: Of-chains work for every relation Ben has taught, which covers the director's 'employer of Ana's boss' case and the whole class it belongs to.
findings.risk: The notebook-closed list could make a new rewrite fire on a phrase like 'the capital of X's king' if 'capital' was ever taught. That is acceptable, since it then answers from taught facts or says don't know. Bench 0-new-wrong must be re-checked.

findings.title: Two bad writes and three wrong routes from keyword matching
findings.problem: Some turns save a wrong value or get routed to the wrong answer. (a) "Anwar's dog is named Pip." stores dog = 'named Pip'. (b) 'My birthday is in March.' stores birthday as an ENTITY (March treated like a person), and then 'When is my birthday?' -> 'You never taught me their age'. (c) The self-question router (keyword-bag scoring, fable_self105.py) grabs statements: 'My favourite colour is teal.' -> 'I do not have favourites.', so the user's fact is dropped with a reply about the assistant. 'Who made you?' and 'What is your name?' -> 'You never told me your name' (187b fixes those two). 'What do you know about me?' -> the user-name reply. (d) 'Forget where Rhea lives.' -> "I don't know anyone called where Rhea." and 'What's Anwar's dog called?' -> "I don't know Anwar's dog called." read question words as part of a name.
findings.evidence: events.jsonl in scratch run1/d03: FACT dog value {'literal': 'named Pip'}. run1/d06: FACT birthday value {'entity': 'E0002'}. Replies as quoted in run1.txt. scripts/fable_self105.py:13-35 describes keyword-overlap routing with typo tolerance, which runs before any statement check.
findings.improvement: (1) Value screen: strip a leading 'named/called' from values and never make month or date words entities (one screen rule each, or one 'value type' rule). (2) Run the self router only on question-shaped turns (starts with a question word or auxiliary, or ends with '?'). 188 already has _QWORDS188/_AUX188 sets to reuse. (3) In the name-slot regexes, reject names that start with a lowercase function word ('where', 'the', 'called'), and give the generic statement fallback instead of 'I don't know anyone called ...'.
findings.expected_gain: Removes every bad write and every false self-answer seen in my probe. The bad writes matter most, because the notebook is the source of truth and sleep later consolidates what is in it.
findings.risk: Low. These are narrower guards. The 138f-h suites expect 'I do not have favourites.' for a self favourite QUESTION (fable_fix138g_suites.py:421), so the guard must keep question-shaped favourite asks routed.

findings.title: The glued fallback is written for the scorers, not for Ben
findings.problem: The unknown-turn reply glues two sentences together on purpose: HONEST_DECLINE plus DECLINE_SUFFIX. The comment says this is so that the bench scorer and the self scorer both count it as an abstain. The result is one confusing reply served for greetings ('Hi there!'), statements ('Pavel is a dentist.'), small talk ('How are you?', 'Tell me a joke.') and world questions ('What's the capital of Peru?'). In my natural batch it was the reply to 23 of 53 turns. 188 (verified, not merged) splits off statement-shaped turns, but it still carries 'don't know' / 'another way' markers kept for the frozen judges.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_loop138_agent.py:85-93 (comment: 'HONEST_DECLINE is scored WRONG by the bench scorer ... appends the redteam/bench abstain bits'). scripts/fable_loop188_agent.py:77-89 (STATEMENT_FALLBACK188 keeps shared abstain markers for 'frozen mechanical judges'). Probe run_188.txt: 12 of my statement turns get the 188 statement sentence instead.
findings.improvement: Fix the judges, not the reply. Give the frozen scorers one shared abstain detector that accepts a short list of approved decline sentences, so each reply can be a single clear sentence by turn type. Question: "I don't know that — you haven't taught me." Statement: "I couldn't save that. Try: 'Kim's boss is Lee.'" Greeting or small talk: a friendly line (156c). World fact: "I only know what you teach me." Re-score old runs with the new detector to show no verdict flips.
findings.expected_gain: Much better demo impression (the uncle/dad demo will surely start with 'Hi'), with no change in any registered verdict if done as a scorer-equivalence step.
findings.risk: Touching frozen scorers can look like goalpost moving. Register it as its own experiment whose only mark is 'old verdicts unchanged under the new detector'.

findings.title: One sealed piece per phrasing does not scale; add a standing fresh-natural-English mark
findings.problem: Each gap the director finds becomes a new piece, a seal, a verification and a later merge layer, and the queue keeps growing: 189c, 'about' widening, reverse widening, 187c, and more on the board's QUEUED line. Pieces pass their own case sets 100% (for example 164b A1 50/50, 190b R1 15/15), but those sets are written by the piece's author around its own pattern, so they do not measure coverage. No mark tracks 'fraction of fresh natural turns handled'. Merges also force odd adapter code (138i re-implements 154c/154e and 172 hears as wrappers because their lineages cannot stack). The ears MRO is 35 classes across 29 files, and the loop MRO is 21 classes.
findings.evidence: MRO probe (scratch wf-loop-parser/mro.py): Loop138iEars 35 classes / 29 files, Loop138iAgentLoop 21 / 18, 109 modules, 35,969 lines, 206 re.compile, 59 'def hear'. Board line 7 (NEXT layer C: 12 pieces) and line 8 (QUEUED phrasing gaps). scripts/fable_loop138i_agent.py:10-30 (wrapper re-implementations).
findings.improvement: Add a standing registered mark on every merge: a fresh natural-English panel of about 100 turns, written by an agent that has not seen the code, across teach/ask/yes-no/correct/forget/pronoun/two-fact/self/small-talk, graded OK/wrong/unhelpful, with bad writes counted. Report the number per merge, with bars of 0 bad writes and the unhelpful rate trending down. Refresh the panel each time so it cannot be tuned to. Then batch phrasing gaps into the lexicon (finding 1) instead of opening a new piece for each.
findings.expected_gain: Gives a real coverage number (my estimate for 138i: about 34% OK on natural turns). It shows whether merges help Ben's actual experience and stops the whack-a-mole pattern.
findings.risk: Grading replies as OK or unhelpful needs a clear rubric. Use a fixed rubric and two graders, or the director's spot check.

findings.title: Missing inverse relations and 'Who is X?' answers
findings.problem: After "Pavel's wife is Mireya.", 'Who is Mireya's husband?' -> "I don't know Mireya's husband." and 'Who is Pavel married to?' -> fallback. After 'My sister is called Liora.', 'Who is Liora?' -> fallback, though the notebook knows she is the user's sister. Reversal is one of Ben's benchmark targets.
findings.evidence: run1.txt dialogs 00 and 01. 190/190b add 'whose'-shaped reverse asks ('Who lives in Lima?') but not symmetric kin pairs.
findings.improvement: Add a small fixed inverse table (wife<->husband, spouse, parent<->child, sibling), used only at ASK time as a derived answer labelled as inferred ('From what you taught me, Mireya's husband is Pavel.'). Never write it as a taught fact. 'Who is X?' lists the facts pointing to X (164b's about-stage already does this for 'Tell me about X').
findings.expected_gain: Shows reversal in the demo and fits the benchmark goal. The hard rule holds because inferences stay unstored and labelled.
findings.risk: Gendered inverses (husband/wife) are an assumption; use them only when the taught relation itself is gendered. It must be a hand-written table, not a learned guess.

keep_as_is: The canonical template path is solid: teach, ask, two-hop possessive ('Rhea's manager's city'), and ask-first corrections ('I have Rhea's city as Ghent. Do you want me to change it to Antwerp?'), then 'Actually, ...' applies it and forget works. No wrong fact was served as an answer in 93 probe turns.
Honest abstention is the default: unknown things get 'I don't know ...' rather than a guess (only the wording needs fixing).

The cooperative-mixin rule 'unclaimed turns fall through untouched', plus predicting every reply move by id before the seal, makes merges safe and auditable. 138i's 0-new-wrong over 800 bench items is real. Keep that discipline for the new parser (parity against sealed suites).
Clear 'Saved: ...' echoes after every teach, so Ben can see exactly what was stored.
Name teaching and user facts ('My name is Juno.' -> saved and recalled) and the 'What can you do?' self-description.
The notebook event log makes bad writes easy to audit (that is how I found the 'named Pip' and 'March as entity' writes).
open_questions_for_ben: Should the English parse stay hand-written for the demo (one clean grammar table, fast to build), or should effort go to the learned ears (ears47 / 119h) doing the parse, with the rules as a fallback? The final system must be your own architecture, so the table could also become the training-label source for the learned ears.

May the frozen scorers get one shared 'approved decline sentences' detector, so replies can be one clear sentence instead of two glued ones? It would be registered as its own experiment whose only mark is 'no old verdict changes'.
For the uncle/dad demo, which 10-15 sentence shapes must work? ('I live in ...', 'X is a dentist', 'How old is X?', pronouns, two facts in one message.) Those should go first into the lexicon.
Is a derived-but-labelled inverse answer ('From what you taught me, Mireya's husband is Pavel') acceptable under the rule that inferences never overwrite taught facts, as long as it is never stored?

summary: The benchmark evidence is one table (exp 125). The rule-based loop, reading English, beats SmolLM2-360M-Instruct on 200 Fable-Edit items (150 correct, 50 abstain, 0 wrong vs 52 correct, 148 wrong) and on 200 fresh 4-hop MQuAKE-Remastered items (loop113b 145/50/5 vs 52/0/148; exp 132 later cut misunderstood questions to 1 of 200 on a new split). The edit and multi-hop part is real: taught facts go in one at a time, a correction replaces the old value, and a symbolic walk follows the chain. My probe on the current base 138i reproduced this (a 'capital of Vesk' correction flowed into the two-hop answer). But the comparison is not fair enough yet for an expert. (1) The 50-item reversal split is broken: every question is ungrammatical or backwards, and on 25 of them the 'gold' answer is the entity named in the question. That gave the loop 50/50 for semantically wrong answers and cost SmolLM about 23 points. (2) SmolLM gets the old fact and the edited fact as an unordered list with no 'later facts replace earlier ones' cue, and 27 of its 66 wrong two-hop answers name the pre-edit answer that was in that list. (3) The loop's side of the comparison is a hand-written regex/grammar parser plus a Python triple store; no learned part runs on the bench path. The learned reasoner (exp 44) and the plain-transformer length comparison (length-eval has no RESULTS) have never been compared against a baseline. The honest claim today is 'a symbolic teachable memory stays at 0 wrong where a small LM reading the same facts guesses'. Claiming 'our model beats a same-size transformer' needs the fixes below.

findings.title: Reversal split is malformed and its scores are wrong for both arms
findings.problem: All 50 reversal questions come from a broken template. Half read like 'Who is the composer of Gilded Mirrors?' with gold 'Gilded Mirrors' (the answer is in the question and backwards). The other half read like 'Who composed by Gilded Mirrors?' (ungrammatical). The loop's reversal 50/50 rewards the backwards answer. SmolLM's 18/50 marks its sensible answers as wrong. It is also not a reversal test at all: both directions are taught explicitly ('X is the composer of Y' and 'Y was composed by X'), so it is a plain lookup.
findings.evidence: data/open/bench65/fable_edit_200.jsonl: 25 of 50 reversal items have gold inside the question (my count). Loop113b row: 'Who is the composer of Gilded Mirrors?' -> "Damon Moonrake's composer of is Gilded Mirrors." scored correct. SmolLM in-context gave the sensible other entity on 23 of those 25 inverted items, all scored wrong. On the other 25 it got 18 correct. So its fair reversal score is about 41/50, not 18/50 (raglite: 23 + 12). scripts/fable_loop113_agent.py:81 has _WHO_BY_RE = r"Who (\w+) by (.+?)\??", a regex written for the broken template. Probe on base 138i: after 'Damon Moonrake is the composer of Gilded Mirrors.', asking 'Who composed Gilded Mirrors?' -> 'I do not know...' and 'What did Damon Moonrake compose?' -> 'I do not know...'.
findings.improvement: Retire the bench65 reversal rows from every table and footnote exp 66/125. Build a true reversal split: teach ONE direction in natural English ('Damon Moonrake composed Gilded Mirrors'), then ask the other way ('Who composed Gilded Mirrors?' / 'What did Damon Moonrake compose?'), with a checker script that proves the gold is not in the question. Seal it, then run the loop and SmolLM on it. This is a real architectural edge (the reversal curse), but the probe shows the current loop fails it too. So the first honest result may be a FAIL, followed by one fix (store the inverse relation when a fact is taught).
findings.expected_gain: Removes a result an expert would find in minutes and that would discredit the whole table. Turns reversal into a real claim that fits the architecture.
findings.risk: Low. The loop's reversal number will fall at first. That is the honest outcome.

findings.title: SmolLM baseline is handicapped by an unordered contradictory fact list
findings.problem: The loop receives facts one at a time, and a later fact replaces an earlier one for the same slot. SmolLM gets 'Facts: - The official language of Spain is Spanish - The official language of Spain is Arabic' with no order cue and no instruction. Many of its 'wrong' answers are the old fact, which is a reasonable reading of an ambiguous prompt. The scorer also counted SmolLM's own hedges ('unknown') as wrong; the director's recount fixed this only partly.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_bench66_baselines.py:134-139 (prompt = bullet list + question; SYSTEM_LINE line 52 says nothing about updates). My recount: on edit200, 27 of SmolLM's wrong two-hop answers name the pre-edit answer; on the 4-hop split, 37 of 148 wrongs do. artifacts/claude-bench125-fairness-20260922/fairness.json moves 11/1/12/12 items from wrong to abstain.
findings.improvement: Add a fair-prompt arm (one change): facts numbered in teaching order, edits marked 'Update: ... (this replaces the earlier fact)', a system line saying newer facts override older ones, and a few-shot example of abstaining. Score with a model-neutral scorer (gold-in-answer plus a shared abstain list). Report old and fair arms side by side.
findings.expected_gain: Pre-empts the first fairness attack. The loop will probably still win on 4-hop and abstention, and the win then counts.
findings.risk: The gap shrinks, perhaps a lot on two-hop. That is still worth knowing before showing an expert.

findings.title: The benchmark win is the parser plus a database, not a learned model: missing baselines an expert will ask for
findings.problem: On the bench path, English goes through hand-written patterns and a 662-line deterministic question rewriter, then a symbolic walk over a triple store. The test sentences come from the same generator the rules were tuned on: one template per relation, and exp 92/103 say the cues were tuned on S1-S3. An expert will say 'this is MeLLo with regexes' and ask how a symbolic baseline or a retrieval+decomposition LM baseline does. Neither has been run. The learned reasoner (exp 44, 64 learned numbers) never runs on MQuAKE, and the plain-transformer length comparison was never finished.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_qrewrite132.py (662 lines, no torch, 'plain software, tiny grammar'); scripts/fable_loop113_agent.py:76-81 regexes. Teach sentences use at most 3 surface forms per relation (my count over bench65; e.g. 'S is a citizen of O'). artifacts/fable-bench103-20260921/RESULTS.md: 'cues were still tuned looking at S1–S3'. artifacts/fable-baseline-length-eval-20260920/ has PREDICTIONS.md and RUN.md but no RESULTS. Probe on 138i: 'Tovin Ashgrove wrote Oaken Melodies.' and 'Brisa Kell is the mother of Orrin Kell.' were both not understood, so the relation and phrasing coverage is narrow.
findings.improvement: (a) Paraphrase-robustness split: have Qwen (allowed for practice sentences) or a second template set rewrite teach sentences and questions for a sealed 200-item split that no rule author sees. Run loop vs fair SmolLM and report the drop. (b) Add a MeLLo-style baseline: same SmolLM, decompose the question into hops, retrieve with BM25 per hop, answer. (c) Add a structured-input arm where the exp-44 learned router does the hops over the same notebook triples, so at least one row is 'our learned weights'.
findings.expected_gain: Separates 'architecture advantage' from 'rules fitted to the test templates'. The minimum an expert needs before 'impressive' is on the table.
findings.risk: The paraphrase split will likely show a big drop for the loop. This is the most informative risk.

findings.title: Strongest honest claim: accuracy vs number of edits in memory (scale test)
findings.problem: All current numbers teach 2-8 facts per item in a fresh notebook, which is exactly where a small LM with all facts in context does fine on paper. The notebook's real advantage is that edits pile up without limit and without interference, while in-context and RAG baselines get worse as memory grows (MQuAKE's batch-edit setting). The only batch run so far (exp 92/103, 924/924 after dropping conflicting cases) has no baseline.
findings.evidence: artifacts/fable-bench103-20260921/RESULTS.md A1: 924/924 on a shared notebook, p50 2.2 ms, with no baseline. Exp 66: RAG-lite already scores below in-context at 8 sentences (33 vs 52 on 4-hop), because top-3 drops bridge facts. Board entry 170: asks at 15k facts in p50 28 ms.
findings.improvement: One registered experiment: k in {1, 10, 100, 1000, 3000} MQuAKE-Remastered cases taught into ONE memory. Arms: loop; SmolLM2-360M with BM25 top-k; SmolLM2 with MeLLo-style per-hop retrieval; optionally SmolLM2-1.7B as a bigger-model reference. Metric: multi-hop accuracy plus the wrong-answer rate at each k. Use MQuAKE-Remastered's own conflict-free subset, so cross-case slot conflicts do not muddy it. SmolLM inference on the 5070 Ti (when free) or the Mac for 360M, no training, well under $30 (likely $0).
findings.expected_gain: A curve an expert recognises from the MQuAKE and MeLLo papers, where the architecture should win clearly and for a principled reason.
findings.risk: Cross-case conflicts (exp 92 lesson) must be removed by rule, not by hand. The loop also needs the phrasing coverage from finding 3, or it is only a structured-input result.

findings.title: Abstention items are trivially detectable
findings.problem: The 'absent' abstention questions name an entity never mentioned. The 'broken' ones contain the literal words 'never-taught relation'. A string match gets 50/50, so the abstention score shows almost nothing about calibrated refusal.
findings.evidence: bench65 row: 'What is the never-taught relation of the apprentice of Quillan Yarwood?' gold []. Absent row: 'Who is the apprentice of Elowen Nettlestone?' where Elowen appears in no taught sentence. Exp 65 notes all broken items were labelled MISSING_FACT, never BROKEN_CHAIN.
findings.improvement: Harder abstention split: known entity with a known relation that is simply not taught for that entity; near-miss names (one letter off from a taught name); chains whose middle hop is missing but whose final relation exists elsewhere; and questions where a real-world prior tempts a guess. Report wrong-answer rate and coverage together (a selective-accuracy style table).
findings.expected_gain: Makes the '0 confident wrongs' claim, the strongest selling point for the demo, stand up to an expert.
findings.risk: Low. The loop may show new wrongs on near-miss names.

findings.title: Unused public data already on disk: TwoHopFact
findings.problem: TwoHopFact.csv (Yang et al. 2024, the latent two-hop reasoning dataset) was downloaded and hash-recorded but never sampled. It gives many natural two-hop prompts over real Wikidata facts without edits: a second, independent two-hop source not built by the project's own generator. It is also the dataset where small LMs are known to fail at composing two facts ('two-hop curse').
findings.evidence: data/open/bench65/raw/TwoHopFact.csv (94.6 MB, sha 522d37...). artifacts/fable-bench65-20260921/RESULTS.md: 'TwoHopFact.csv was downloaded ... but not sampled'.
findings.improvement: Sealed split of 200-500 TwoHopFact items: teach the two facts in the dataset's own wording, ask the two-hop question, and compare the loop with fair-prompt SmolLM (in-context) and closed-book SmolLM (to measure pretraining leakage). No download needed. Other cheap public options if Ben approves a download: the reversal-curse celebrity parent/child pairs (Berglund et al.) and MQuAKE-T or RippleEdits.
findings.expected_gain: A second, externally built dataset with its own phrasing. This directly tests the 'templated data' attack at zero cost.
findings.risk: Real-world names clash with the 'fictional names only in tests' rule. This needs Ben's ruling on benchmark data (MQuAKE already uses real names).

keep_as_is: The sealing and pre-registration discipline (PASSMARKS sha, ledger predictions, fresh blind splits with zero case_id overlap as in bench103/132). An expert will respect this more than any single number.
Every item gets a fresh isolated notebook, taught through the real English path (bench113 run_item). It measures the real system, not a shortcut.
Exp 125's 'What it does not mean' section already states the leakage and scorer-mismatch caveats honestly. Keep that style for any claim shown to Ben's uncle or an expert.
The director's fairness recount (claude-bench125-fairness) is the right habit. Make neutral scoring the default, not a patch.
Last-writer-wins correction plus multi-hop walk works end to end on base 138i (probe: the Vesk capital correction flowed into the two-hop answer).
Using MQuAKE-Remastered CF3k (the cleaned version) rather than the original MQuAKE was the right source choice.
open_questions_for_ben: Benchmark data from public sets (MQuAKE, TwoHopFact) uses real people's names. Is that an allowed exception to 'fictional names only in tests', or should entities be renamed to fictional ones (which also removes SmolLM's pretraining advantage and leakage)?

For the expert claim, is it acceptable for the headline row to be the symbolic loop (a 'system' result), with learned components as extra rows? Or must the winning row be learned weights (for example the exp-44 router on MQuAKE triples)?
May an agent use Qwen to paraphrase teach sentences and questions for a sealed robustness split, given that Qwen-written practice sentences were already allowed for the ears?

summary: The director's worry is a false alarm, but it points at a real hole. Live sleep IS in the current base: build_agent138i calls S145.retrofit_sleep145 (scripts/fable_loop138i_agent.py:423-429), which swaps in Sleep145Reasoner and Sleep145Sleeper. The marks123 message "no Sleep104Daemon" comes from a plain text search for that name. Worse, the marks123 SLEEP suite skips and reports pass=True whichever way that search goes, and the harness's make_daemon sets sleep_threshold=100000, so no merge since 138b has ever run sleep. I turned the threshold back on in a Mac probe (the exp-104 world through the 138i daemon, 86 turns). Sleep fired by itself at turn 76 and took 69 s. It installed maternal_grandmother (20 episodes, OOF 1.00, agreement 1.00, 0 wrong installs), and answered 5/5 new people it had never been asked about. Before sleep it answered 0/20 of the same questions, even though both hops were taught. What actually goes into weights is small: a 3x9 table of routing numbers per word (which of the 8 frozen relation skills to chain together). The reasoner uses that table to walk the notebook (fix77_core.py:249-251). No facts are ever put into weights, so answers do not survive losing the notebook. The biggest honesty gap: the practice answers come from hard-coded chains (CHAINS130). Sleep rediscovers a definition the code already contains, instead of learning from what Ben teaches. The toy results for putting facts into weights (rank-4 limit, CardFold replay) never reached the live loop, and should not yet, because of the length wall.

findings.title: Merge gate never tests sleep (SLEEP mark is always SKIP and counted as pass)
findings.problem: suite_sleep in marks123 writes skipped=True, pass=True in both branches of its only if-statement. Separately, make_daemon forces sleep_threshold=100000 for every suite (and for the probe harness dialog_full.py), so sleep can never fire in any merge test. The 138b-138i SLEEP lines ('no Sleep104Daemon') are a name search, not a finding that sleep is absent. So sleep145 inside 138i has never been checked by a merge.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_marks123_all.py:694-711 (both branches pass=True); :99-103 make_daemon sets cfg['sleep_threshold']=100000; artifacts/fable-agent138{b,d,f,g,h,i}-*/marks*/sleep-report.json all carry the same skip reason. Probe: in-process 138i daemon, 60 turns: sleep_threshold=100000, experience 60, sleep_mark 0 (never slept).
findings.improvement: Replace suite_sleep with a real smoke mark. Use one fresh 138i daemon with sleep_threshold set to 76, run the exp-104 world (50 teaches, 20 maternal-grandmother asks, 1 broken-chain teach, 4 fillers), then check: exactly 1 sleep, installed=1, bridged, 5/5 new-people probes right with source sleep-derived, broken chain gives an honest 'I don't know N06's mother', taught rows untouched, 0 overwrites. It takes about 75 s on the Mac. Also correct the board: 138i does include live sleep (sleep145).
findings.expected_gain: Every later merge (138j onward) actually protects sleep. Right now a merge could break sleep and still report SLEEP PASS.
findings.risk: Adds about 75 s to the marks wave. The smoke world must stay fictional and fixed (K/M/G/T/N/H names, as in exp 104).

findings.title: Sleep's teaching signal is circular: labels come from hard-coded chains, not from Ben
findings.problem: Every episode queue (104/115/130 reasoners, wire51 adapters) builds its 'answer' by walking a hard-coded chain in the notebook (CHAINS130, e.g. maternal_grandmother = mother+mother). So the program already knows the definition it then 'learns'. Word facts Ben teaches directly (e.g. 'K01's maternal grandmother is G01') are never used as practice data; they are only answered back as taught (the 131/145 rule). The word list is closed (12 words), and a synonym is unknown: 'Who is T01's grandmother?' gives I don't know, even after the install. Exp 104's own driver notes that wrong teaches before the asks are invisible to the gate for this reason, and exp 116 family F shows the same thing.
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_sleep130_agent.py:85-112 (WORDS130/CHAINS130), :153-170 (_queue130 walks CHAINS130[w]); grep: every episodes.append site (sleep104:120, sleep115:172, sleep130:169, wire51_adapters:406,426) is a chain walk; scripts/fable_sleep104_drive.py:64-72 docstring; probe turn 82 'Who is T01's grandmother?' -> "I don't know T01's grandmother."
findings.improvement: One change: take episodes from TAUGHT compound-word rows. When Ben has taught 'X's <word> is Y' for enough people, and the single hops for those people are also in the notebook, each (X, word, Y) becomes an episode. The router (the exp-46 recipe, unchanged, plus 130's grow-one-slot for a new word name) then finds, by gradient descent, which chain of known relations reproduces Ben's answers. Chains are no longer hard-coded; the fixed chain table stays only as a hidden scoring key in tests. This keeps 'automatic + mathematical': a fixed count formula decides when a word is ready, and gradient descent finds the routing. The model proposes nothing.
findings.expected_gain: Sleep becomes real learning from Ben's English teaching: he defines a new word by example ('Pim's nana is Ada' x ~10-20 people), and after sleep it answers for strangers where only the hops were taught. This is the teachable-assistant goal and a strong demo moment. It also lets the noise gate see a wrong teach, because Ben's label and the notebook walk can disagree.
findings.risk: A new word needs an ears path that turns an unknown relation name into a relation token (open-vocabulary teach). Ben needs 10-20 examples per word (exp 104 used 20; the exp-46 gate held with 8 in exp 116 T1). Taught facts must stay unchanged, so the taught-wins rule from 145 stays.

findings.title: Be exact about what sleep stores: word definitions (27 routing numbers), not facts
findings.problem: Sleep's bridge copies the hardened [3][9] logits for one word into reasoner.inner.words and sleep145-words.json. At answer time fix77_core turns them into stage options and walks the notebook. No taught fact goes into weights, and nothing answers without the notebook. Probe: after install, the broken chain T06 (mother taught, grandmother hop missing) gave "I don't know N06's mother." The toy results that do put knowledge into weights (43E rank-4 on the CardFold transformer, CardFold lesson practice, exp-42 raw replay) are not wired in anywhere live, and they still hit the length wall (CardFold M3 1-11%, 43E long inputs <=0.05).
findings.evidence: scripts/fable_sleep115_agent.py:306-340 (_commit_one: sd['words.{w}'] -> self.reasoner.inner.words[wname]); scripts/fable_fix77_core.py:249-251; probe run2: turns 76-80 5/5 correct, turn 81 abstains on the missing hop; memory exp43e, cardfold-sleep-result, exp42.
findings.improvement: Say it in the demo and in docs: 'Sleep learns what a new relation word means by practising on examples, then applies it to people it has never seen.' Do not say 'sleep puts facts into weights'. Do not wire rank-4/CardFold-style weight updates into the base until a length-generalisation fix exists. Keep them as toy results.
findings.expected_gain: Claims no bigger than the evidence (Ben's rule). The uncle/dad demo stays truthful, and an expert will not catch an overclaim.
findings.risk: None. It is wording plus a decision not to wire something in.

findings.title: A test that would convincingly show sleep helps
findings.problem: Current marks show that the install happens and generalises to 5 new people, but there is no comparison with anything outside our own system, and no test that the learned definition persists. Exp 104 Z4 showed that a finished install reloads after a restart (5/5), but not that it survives losing the notebook.
findings.evidence: artifacts/fable-sleep104-20260921/RESULTS.md Z2/Z4 rows; artifacts/fable-sleep130-20260922 G1 25/25; no plain-transformer arm in any fable-sleep* RESULTS (grep of listed artifacts).
findings.improvement: Run one registered experiment with three arms on the same 20 taught examples (after the circular-labels fix): (a) our loop after one automatic sleep; (b) the same loop with sleep disabled (the notebook alone gives 0/20, as seen in this probe); (c) the plain baseline-v2 transformer of equal size, fine-tuned on the same 20 examples plus the hop facts. Measure: new-people accuracy where only hops are taught; the same after the notebook is wiped and only the new people's hops are re-taught, with no new sleep (the definition should survive, because sleep145-words.json persists); and 3-hop words (doctor_of_mothers_friend) on new people. Three seeds, reported separately.
findings.expected_gain: A clean 'advantage over a plain transformer' result on Mac CPU, costing $0: learning from about 20 examples, then applying the lesson to strangers and keeping it after the notebook is lost. This is exactly the demo and benchmark story.
findings.risk: The transformer arm might do well on 2-hop words with 20 examples (baseline v2 already fits 1-3 hops with a hint). If so, the honest result is 'no advantage at 2 hops', and the 3-hop and persistence columns carry the claim.

findings.title: Sleep blocks the user's turn for about 70 s
findings.problem: The sleep fires inside the turn that fills the log. In the probe, 'Good morning!' took 69.0 s to answer, because the install ran before the reply. With the live config's sleep_threshold=20, this can hit any turn once episodes are waiting. That is bad for conversation-first use.
findings.evidence: Probe run2 turn 75: 'Good morning!' ... [69.0s]; last_outcome sleep_seconds 69.01; artifacts/fable-agent138i-20260922/loop138i-config.json sleep_threshold 20; fable_agent_loop.py:288 (sleep check after the log grows).
findings.improvement: Keep the trigger fixed and automatic (log size), but reply first and then sleep, or sleep in the daemon's idle tick with a status line like 'sleeping...'. The kill-mid-sleep safety from exp 104 Z4 must keep holding.
findings.expected_gain: Chat stays responsive; sleep feels like a background process, which also demos better.
findings.risk: Changes the timing of the exactly-once/receipts path in the daemon, so the soak and kill-9 marks must be re-run.

findings.title: The 138i config still describes the old sleeper
findings.problem: The config's sleeper block says 'HardGate46Sleeper ... episode feed idle until learned-word asks' and names wire57 as the install path. The built agent actually uses Sleep145Sleeper plus Sleep145Reasoner (grow-slot, taught-wins). Stale text like this is probably what misled the director.

keep_as_is: The exp-46 recipe as the live install (robust loss, harden-before-gate, unchanged 0.80/0.90 gate): in the 138i probe it gave OOF 1.00, agreement 1.00, 0 wrong installs.
The 145 taught-beats-sleep rule: a directly taught fact always wins over a sleep-derived answer (fixes exp-116 family E). This matches the rule that taught facts are never overwritten.
